paragraphs: When researchers transferred gut bacteria from obese mice into germ-free mice, the recipients gained more fat than germ-free mice given bacteria from lean donors, even though both groups ate the same diet. The result has been widely cited as showing that gut bacteria help cause obesity. It does show that bacteria can influence weight gain under laboratory conditions. But what holds in mice under laboratory conditions need not hold in people, whose diets, genes and lifetimes of exposure to microbes vary enormously. Moreover, the experiment cannot reveal whether in free-living animals the bacteria are a cause of obesity or merely a consequence of the eating habits that accompany it.
